method.protocol: static T=0 K energy-volume scan of the 8-atom conventional diamond cell, isotropic strain, fitted with a Birch-Murnaghan EOS (ase.eos); Vinet and Murnaghan fits used as cross-checks
method.eos_points: 11 volumes at +/-3% linear strain (also checked +/-6% n=11 and +/-2% n=7)

payload.note: a0 = 5.4559 A (BM, +/-3%). Spread across EOS forms (BM/Vinet/Murnaghan) and strain windows (+/-2/3/6%) is 5.4556-5.4569 A, so fit error is about 0.001 A. A 64-atom 2x2x2 supercell gives the same numbers, so the result has no size dependence. Uncertainty 0.03 A (about 0.5%) is the model-vs-experiment systematic error, estimated from validation: the same pipeline gives diamond C a0 = 3.5707 A against the commonly quoted 3.567 A (+0.1%) and Ge a0 = 5.7735 A against 5.658 A (+2.0%, the PBE-typical overestimate inherited from the MACE-MP training data). The C and Ge reference values are standard textbook numbers that I did not web-verify in this run. For Si itself, NIST SRM 640c certifies a = 5.431195 A at 295.6 K, so this result is +0.46% (+0.025 A) above experiment, which is consistent with PBE-level overbinding. The calculation is a static-lattice result: it leaves out zero-point and thermal expansion, which are small for Si (<~0.1%). Bulk modulus B = 74.5 GPa.
